free_text: The 82-year-old male presents with an elevated PSA of 14.0 ng/mL and a prior diagnosis of prostate adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 5+5 (ISUP grade group 5). The mpMRI showed a focal lesion in the right peripheral zone with restricted diffusion, but no extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion was identified. Given the high-grade disease and patient age, the management assessment focuses on individual treatment benefit and patient preferences, balancing potential cancer control against treatment side effects.
